A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GLoTran/GLoD, with readable text, equations, figures and tables. Neither contains an appendix despite references to one: v1 cites 'Appendix ??' for baseline details, while v2 cites 'Appendix 10' for detector details. Those promised technical details cannot be compared.

before.justification: v1 reports original GLoTran benchmark results, backbone and sensitivity experiments, efficiency measurements and qualitative translation comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds fine-tuning controls, detector-assisted comparisons and component ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 changes the reported crop-processing sequence from ordering before merging to merging before content ordering, with MinerU suggested. The detector is newly described as self-trained at block/paragraph level, although its unavailable details prevent establishing the implementation change. Dual-view encoding, cross-attention, replay and the loss remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The documented coverage remains GLoD training, MCiTon English-to-Chinese scenarios and the same MTIT6 language tasks. Added controls reuse these datasets. Removing one qualitative poster example does not remove poster-domain coverage.

E2.justification: v2 retains the original comparators but adds GLoD-fine-tuned InternVL3 8B and Qwen3-VL 8B in Table 2. New Table 4 also evaluates detector-assisted InternVL3, Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL. These are focused extensions using adapted versions of existing baselines.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce plain GLoD fine-tuning, a LoRA-labelled configuration, detector-cropped inputs, PSC cropping and global-image/replay removal controls. Section 5.2 drops METEOR from the stated metrics; BLEU/COMET and the existing main training budget remain. The newly disclosed 99:1 split does not establish that the split changed.

E4.justification: v1 already tested backbones, resolution, replay-window size and efficiency. v2 substantially expands diagnostic evidence through data-only fine-tuning controls and tests isolating localization, text-aware versus PSC cropping, global context and replay contributions in Tables 2 and 4. Figure 6 removes the poster case and adds error annotations to the retained GLoTran menu example.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests. Point-estimate reporting continues unchanged.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark, backbone, efficiency and sensitivity scores are retained, while Tables 2 and 4 add substantial condition-specific results. For example, the new global-image ablation reports News BLEU/COMET of 44.8/83.7 against the retained full-model 57.5/88.6. Figure 6 removes one example and newly marks GLoTran menu mistranslations. The new LoRA and no-replay rows have identical eight-scenario scores, leaving their attribution unclear.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 revises the formal slice construction from M(ord(crops)) to ord(M(crops)), matching the changed processing order. The formal TIMT objective and Equations 1–4 otherwise remain unchanged; no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The core contributions remain the global-local GLoTran framework, the approximately 510K-pair GLoD dataset and improved translation completeness and accuracy. The abstract now explicitly mentions replay, but replay was already part of v1.

C2.justification: v2 newly interprets GLoD-only fine-tuning as insufficient and potentially harmful in complex scenes. It also attributes PSC degradation to irrelevant regions, fragmented text and missed small text. Existing explanations of model scaling and resolution/replay sensitivity are retained.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses 512,180 training and 5,174 validation pairs, no image overlap with the evaluation datasets, and benchmark resolution distributions. Conversely, it removes v1's eight NVIDIA A100 80GB GPU disclosure. The self-trained detector refers to an unavailable appendix, and the LoRA configuration is unspecified.

R1.justification: Section 2 expands positioning against existing global-local perception approaches, including V*, ZoomEye, attention-based selection and Divide, Conquer and Combine, distinguishing holistic queries from ordered translation. MinerU and mPLUG-DocOwl2 references are also added, while the METEOR reference is removed. The broader TIMT positioning remains.

P1.justification: The six-section organization and most prose remain intact. Rewriting concentrates on related work, preprocessing and complexity discussion, alongside added experimental paragraphs. Affiliations and contact details change, and keywords, a corresponding-author note and acknowledgements are added.

P2.justification: The paper changes from two-column to single-column layout with extensive resizing and relocation. Figures 1 and 3 are rearranged, Figure 4 replaces platform logos with generic source categories, and v1 Figures 5 and 7 merge into v2 Figure 5. Figure 6 is shortened and reannotated; Table 2 expands and a new component table is added.

improvement.justification: The added fine-tuning and component controls address validation gaps, while split and non-overlap disclosures improve transparency. However, the unexplained identical LoRA and no-replay results in Tables 2 and 4 weaken the interpretability of part of this evidence; the LoRA aggregate is also unexplained by its scene scores. Missing detector details and removed hardware information further limit reproducibility. These competing changes prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
